question: to the Commission Markus Buchheit (ESN) Subject:

Since the guidelines for developing a Trans-European Transport Network (TEN-T) were adopted in 1996, the Commission has been working towards the related objectives. The standardisation of the future railway mobile communication system (FRMCS) – which is to be based on 5G technology instead of the outdated GSM-R standard – began in 2015, and the requirements specification was completed in 2020. Despite this preparatory work having started years ago, the FRMCS remains at the pilot and testing stage across the EU. There are no plans for seamless, full-scale operation in any Member State before 2028; in several cases, not before 2035. 1.
How does the Commission explain the fact that, ten years after the start of standardisation work, the FRMCS is still not operational across the EU?
By when exactly does it expect the FRMCS to operate seamlessly and uniformly throughout the EU? Which Member States would it say are currently lagging behind?
